papers.title: Mix Forcing: Causal Pre-Training via Mixture Attention for Interactive World Models
papers.abstract: While interactive video world models require autoregressive generation, directly adapting pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into autoregressive ones with teacher forcing can disrupt their visual priors and degrade autoregressive generation quality. In this paper, we introduce Mix Forcing, a causal pre-training paradigm for interactive video world models, implemented with the Mixture-of-Bidirectional-and-Autoregressive (MoBA) attention. Mix Forcing jointly trains a video diffusion model with both teacher forcing and bidirectional training, yielding a strong causal initialization for few-step post-training. In self-attention, Mix Forcing leverages teacher forcing to learn causal next-chunk prediction for autoregressive rollout, while using bidirectional attention to preserve pretrained visual priors. To support online text interaction, Mix Forcing further adopts a chunk-wise cross-attention design that conditions each video chunk on a shared environment prompt and its own local prompt, without exposing future instructions to the current chunk. Following causal pre-training on a 14B image-to-video model, we apply consistency and distribution matching distillation to obtain a four-step autoregressive generator. Experiments on our internal benchmark and public benchmarks, including WBench and SANA-WM-Bench, show that our model achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and timely event following with precise camera control. Notably, our model supports high-fidelity long-horizon generation without quality degradation even over one-hour rollouts. Project page is here: https://zelingao98.github.io/mixforcing

papers.title: BoxWorld: Let World Engines Control and Video Generators Render
papers.abstract: We tackle the challenge of building real-time interactive video worlds with user-defined behaviors. Such worlds must track object states, apply interaction rules, and render the resulting consequences as users act. Yet existing end-to-end video world models typically learn interaction dynamics within the generator, making it difficult to specify object-level rules and reason about their consequences. In this work, we introduce BoxWorld, which separates interaction reasoning from generative rendering. Given user-specified rules, a coding agent creates a Box World Engine that determines interaction outcomes and exposes the resulting object states through a lightweight interface of layout boxes, persistent object attributes, and dynamic status variables, leaving appearance and physical effects to generative rendering. A Box-State Generative Renderer then renders this evolving state stream into video autoregressively, enabling online control over object motion, state switches, and conditional events. Rendering this state stream is non-trivial: the renderer must respond to object-level state updates in real time while remaining coherent with the generated history. To this end, we introduce a three-stage training strategy that learns object grounding from open-domain videos and state transitions from gameplay videos, both annotated automatically, and finally performs rollout distillation on self-generated histories. We further propose PairedStateBench, a paired benchmark for fine-grained interaction control. BoxWorld substantially outperforms end-to-end world models and remains competitive across multiple public benchmarks. Project page: https://boxworld-web.github.io.
papers.summary_cn: BoxWorld 将交互规则执行与视频渲染解耦：编码代理根据用户规则生成世界引擎，维护对象状态并决定交互结果；自回归视频渲染器则通过布局框、持久属性和动态状态，将状态流实时生成视频。作者基于开放领域视频和游戏视频的自动标注，采用布局 grounding、状态动态适配和 rollout 蒸馏三阶段训练，并提出 PairedStateBench。实验显示，该方法在条件交互控制、多阶段任务和布局到视频生成方面优于端到端基线，同时以约 20.7 FPS 运行并保持较好的短视频和长视频质量。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 BoxWorld 框架，用编码代理创建的 Box World Engine 显式执行用户定义的交互规则，并通过对象中心状态接口连接交互推理与生成式渲染。 2. 提出 Box-State Generative Renderer，使用逐帧掩码交叉注意力，将对象布局框、持久属性和动态状态注入自回归视频生成，实现异步、因果和在线渲染。 3. 提出三阶段训练策略：Masked Layout Grounding 学习对象定位，State Dynamics Adaptation 学习状态变化，Rollout Distillation 使模型适应自身生成历史并恢复少步推理能力。 4. 通过现成感知模型从开放领域视频和游戏视频自动提取状态标注，无需动作配对的交互日志。 5. 提出 PairedStateBench，用成对分支评估指定后果是否触发、未指定后果是否被抑制以及多阶段任务是否完成。
papers.relevance_cn: 该论文与研究重点高度相关。它面向实时视频生成、交互式视觉世界模型和闭环模拟，将用户动作输入世界引擎，由引擎更新状态，再由视频生成器渲染结果，形成明确的状态驱动闭环。其渲染器采用自回归、因果、异步流式生成，能够在状态更新到达后在线生成后续帧；基于 LongLive 初始化、四步去噪和 rollout 蒸馏，达到约 20.7 FPS。逐帧状态注入、空间掩码交叉注意力以及 LoRA 适配体现了面向实时生成的条件控制、稀疏注意和高效复用思路。与端到端世界模型相比，BoxWorld 将规则推理外置，因此更适合可编程的动作条件模拟和细粒度对象交互控制；不过其外部引擎主要负责状态逻辑，视觉外观与物理效果仍由生成器近似渲染。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确显示，BoxWorld 依赖布局框、持久属性和动态状态等对象级接口，无法直接表达所有细粒度或密集的场景状态；在 YouTube-VIS 上其 mIOU 为 0.572，低于使用更精细 blob 表示的 BlobGEN-Vid（0.598）。状态标注依赖 Grounding DINO、SAM 2、视频描述和对象级字幕等现成感知模型，感知错误可能影响渲染结果。训练中的状态动态适配使用约 4,000 个在线收集的短游戏视频，且状态转移主要来自游戏数据，跨域泛化仍可能受限。编码代理生成的世界引擎能否正确实现复杂或含歧义的用户规则，论文未系统评估。论文也未明确说明在更复杂物理交互、长期记忆、多人交互或大规模对象数量下的性能和稳定性。
papers.abstract_cn: 我们致力于解决构建支持用户自定义行为的实时交互式视频世界这一挑战。这类世界必须跟踪物体状态、应用交互规则，并在用户行动时渲染由此产生的后果。然而，现有端到端视频世界模型通常在生成器内部学习交互动力学，因此难以指定对象级规则并推理其后果。本文提出 BoxWorld，将交互推理与生成式渲染分离。给定用户指定的规则，编码代理创建一个 Box World Engine，用于确定交互结果，并通过由布局框、持久对象属性和动态状态变量组成的轻量级接口暴露产生的对象状态，将外观和物理效果留给生成式渲染。随后，Box-State Generative Renderer 以自回归方式将不断演化的状态流渲染为视频，从而实现对物体运动、状态切换和条件事件的在线控制。渲染这一状态流并非易事：渲染器必须实时响应对象级状态更新，同时与已生成的历史保持连贯。为此，我们提出三阶段训练策略：从开放领域视频中学习对象定位，从游戏视频中学习状态转移（两者均通过自动方式标注），最后在模型自行生成的历史上进行 rollout 蒸馏。我们进一步提出 PairedStateBench，这是一个用于细粒度交互控制的成对基准。BoxWorld 的性能显著超过端到端世界模型，并且在多个公开基准上保持竞争力。项目主页：https://boxworld-web.github.io。

papers.title: UniWorld: A Unified World Model for Real-Time Visual World Simulation
papers.abstract: Continuous visual world simulation requires coupling evolving scene geometry with temporally persistent appearance. We present UniWorld, a unified framework that integrates depth trajectories and reference appearance within a shared video generation model. The central design maintains visual and geometric histories on a common timeline. Noise-aligned overlapping continuation places generated history at the prescribed sampling noise level and commits only newly generated latents. Rolling depth latent state preserves the corresponding geometric controls, incrementally reads newly available geometry, and keeps the conditioning fixed within each sampling window. Together, these mechanisms ensure exact preservation of latent history while bounding the active depth state by the window size. We evaluate continuous generation, paired history interventions, and long-horizon behavior across diverse scene categories. The same generator supports estimated, native, and on-demand simulator depth, while cached and incremental execution paths produce bitwise-identical outputs. Appearance changes and geometric control branches operate through the same interface without modifying committed history. The measured steady-state DiT execution path achieves real-time generation throughput, demonstrating the efficiency of UniWorld for continuous visual world simulation. Project page: https://zephipage.github.io/UniWorld.
papers.summary_cn: UniWorld 面向由外部世界源驱动的连续视觉模拟，将不同来源的几何状态统一转换为图像对齐深度，并与参考图像外观共同输入视频生成器。方法通过噪声对齐的重叠续接保留视频潜变量历史，通过滚动深度潜状态增量读取并固定几何条件，只提交每个窗口的新视频后缀。实验覆盖驾驶、人体活动、模拟和合成场景，表明该方法能够支持长时生成、原生或估计深度、外观切换及控制分支，并在八张 H100 GPU 上的稳态 DiT 路径达到实时吞吐率。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 UniWorld 统一视觉模拟框架，将异构几何轨迹表示为图像对齐深度，并结合参考外观，为记录场景、模拟器和按需世界轨迹提供统一生成渲染接口。2. 提出噪声对齐的重叠续接方法，在每个流时间步约束生成窗口中的历史前缀，仅提交新生成的后缀，从而保持既有潜变量并利用时间上下文继续生成。3. 提出滚动深度潜状态，增量读取新深度位置、保留已提交观测对应的几何条件，并使活动状态上界与序列总时长无关。4. 通过真实模型执行验证历史保持、缓存与在线路径的逐位一致性，并展示多场景、长时和按需控制下的连续视觉模拟能力。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点直接相关：它是一个视频扩散/流匹配生成框架，用于由深度轨迹驱动的视觉世界模拟；通过重叠窗口、噪声历史投影和滚动状态实现因果式的连续、长视频生成。其固定历史、增量读取新几何、缓存复用和有界活动状态机制对应流式生成与缓存复用；DMD 蒸馏后的八步 DiT 以及实测 14.472 FPS（960×544）和 21.361 FPS（672×384）的吞吐率对应实时生成和蒸馏方向。论文还支持模拟器控制分支及按需几何输入，但其生成窗口内部仍采用双向处理，因此并非严格的逐帧自回归模型。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的实时吞吐率是在八张 H100 GPU、FSDP/Ulysses 并行和稳态 DiT 前向路径上测得的，未证明单 GPU、消费级硬件或完整端到端系统都能实时运行。方法依赖输入的参考图像、空间和时间对齐的深度序列，以及可靠的上游模拟器或深度估计器；深度估计误差和跨来源泛化仍可能影响结果。实验主要使用 100 个 30 秒片段，并辅以 60 秒和 120 秒测试，尚未充分验证更长时长或更广泛真实世界分布。长时生成的 PSNR、LPIPS 和几何指标仍会随时间变化，模拟场景的深度 NMAE 明显高于其他类别。论文未明确说明在更复杂交互、快速拓扑变化、遮挡严重或需要物理一致性的环境中的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 连续视觉世界模拟需要将不断演化的场景几何与具有时间持久性的外观结合起来。我们提出 UniWorld，一个统一框架，在共享的视频生成模型中融合深度轨迹与参考外观。其核心设计在同一时间轴上维护视觉历史和几何历史。噪声对齐的重叠续接将生成历史置于规定的采样噪声水平，并只提交新生成的潜变量。滚动深度潜状态保留相应的几何控制，增量读取新获得的几何信息，并在每个采样窗口内保持条件不变。这些机制共同确保潜变量历史得到精确保留，同时将活动深度状态限制在窗口大小以内。我们在连续生成、成对历史干预和跨多种场景类别的长时行为方面进行了评估。同一个生成器支持估计深度、原生深度和按需模拟器深度；缓存执行路径与增量执行路径能够产生逐位一致的输出。外观变化和几何控制分支通过同一接口运行，且不会修改已提交的历史。实测的稳态 DiT 执行路径达到了实时生成吞吐率，展示了 UniWorld 用于连续视觉世界模拟的效率。项目主页：https://zephipage.github.io/UniWorld。

papers.title: OSWAM: An Effective World Action Model with One-Step Action Generation
papers.abstract: Direct-policy World Action Models (WAM) have demonstrated the benefits of decoupling action generation from explicit future visual prediction for efficient inference in autonomous driving and embodied control. However, they still require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, incurring substantial latency and hindering real-time deployment. Simply reducing the number of denoising steps will collapse the nonlinear multi-step denoising trajectory into coarse updates, substantially degrading action quality. To reduce the denoising steps while enabling real-time action generation, we present an effective world action model with one-step action generation, namely OSWAM, for autonomous driving and embodied control. We argue that it is the absence of structured action priors in random noise initialization that forces direct-policy WAMs to recover coherent action sequences through iterative denoising. Hence, we construct imagination tokens to initialize the diffusion process, providing physical priors and action-conditioned representations. We further introduce privileged information distillation with future conditioning to enhance future-aware action generation. As a result, OSWAM can efficiently and effectively generate high quality actions in just one diffusion step. Our experiments demonstrate that OSWAM achieves comparable or even better results in both autonomous driving and embodied control than direct-policy WAM and Joint-WAM that require tens of steps. It obtains approximately $3\times$ speedup over direct-policy WAM baselines and supports real-time compiled inference with latency as low as 40ms on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU. The project page is available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM/

papers.title: FlockWorld: Toward Population-Scale Multi-Agent Video World Models through Artificial Life Simulation
papers.abstract: Most action-conditioned video world models remain limited to a single player, while existing multiplayer models support only small, fixed groups of agents. We introduce FlockWorld, an artificial-life environment built on Reynolds's Boids algorithm for studying population-scale multi-agent video world models. Specifically, FlockWorld renders synchronized egocentric crops, assigns distinct colors to preserve camera-agent identity across views, exposes rule-derived accelerations as actions, and lets the number of camera agents be configured independently of the size of the surrounding population. We further introduce FlockDiT, an action-conditioned latent diffusion transformer trained with flow matching on FlockWorld data to jointly generate synchronized egocentric videos for multiple agents. Our results suggest that joint generation benefits agent detection at density-matched settings and that diffusion forcing improves rollout fidelity. Together, FlockWorld and FlockDiT provide a controlled testbed for multi-agent video generation.

papers.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
papers.abstract: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal interaction histories into structured conditions for the next segment. A multi-stage curriculum progressively introduces causal generation, text interaction, camera control, and training on model-generated histories, followed by diffusion distillation. In human evaluation, Hy-Nomas shows superior performance over existing world models. We release model weights, code and benchmarks, together with a lightweight adaptation workflow, to support reproducible research on interactive world generation.

papers.title: Direct Forcing: Single-Stage Training with Representation-Space Supervision for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generation enables low-latency streaming, yet prevailing training pipelines separate causal adaptation from distribution matching. Recent representation-based text-to-video methods retain this separation by starting with an ODE initialization stage, even when the target distribution is defined directly by reference videos. We introduce \method, the first single-stage framework that uses reference videos both as paired examples of how a history continues and as a target population for self-generated rollouts. Specifically, Direct Forcing is trained with two complementary signals: (1) Causal Continuation Alignment learns paired spatiotemporal correspondence under reference histories; and (2) Rollout Distribution Matching employs maximum mean discrepancy to align the representation distributions of self-generated and reference videos. To coordinate these signals, we introduce Dynamic Gradient Balancing, which adapts their relative gradient contributions during training. Experiments with Wan2.1-1.3B show that Direct Forcing learns a four-step autoregressive generator in 250 updates without a separate ODE initialization stage or online diffusion-score supervision, achieving 84.63 VBench Total and 86.01 Quality.

papers.contribution_cn: We introduce \method, the first single-stage framework that uses reference videos both as paired examples of how a history continues and as a target population for self-generated rollouts.

papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
papers.abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

papers.contribution_cn: We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation.

papers.title: Beyond Distribution Matching: Self-Supervised Representation Forcing for Few-Step Video Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step distillation is essential for deploying modern video diffusion models. Among existing approaches, Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) has emerged as a highly promising paradigm by achieving strong output-space fidelity without adversarial training, while remaining flexible across various student architectures. We observe, however, that DMD fundamentally relies on an output-space objective, lacking explicit regularization on the model's internal representations. As the distillation step count aggressively shrinks, this output-only supervision becomes insufficient, causing the distilled student to degrade in both fine-grained spatial structures and coherent temporal dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce Self Flow Forcing (SF$^2$), which incorporates a predictive representation loss into the DMD framework without altering its output objective. By providing the student and an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) teacher with heterogeneous noise levels, we establish an information asymmetry. This formulation forces the student to predict the teacher's internal representations from a more corrupted input, effectively integrating self-supervised representation alignment into distribution matching. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SF$^2$ effectively mitigates temporal flickering and consistently improves both spatial fidelity and motion quality. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism is architecture-agnostic - seamlessly supporting both bidirectional and causal models - and requires no external feature extractors, introducing minimal computational overhead.

papers.title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
papers.abstract: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications. Spanning 9 diverse scenes, WMEval assesses action controllability, scene and character consistency, prompt adherence, kinematics, fluid mechanics, physical causality, and lighting. By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. Experiments on state-of-the-art models reveal significant room for improvement in dimensions that remain hidden by standard perceptual metrics but are vital for real-world deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/WMEval.
papers.summary_cn: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility.
